instagram_carousel.caption:
New Zealand is just across the Tasman, but the paperwork will not look after itself. Here is how the legal side works for Australian couples.

You do not need to be New Zealand citizens: visitors can marry in New Zealand. You need a marriage licence and a registered celebrant.

1. Choose your celebrant before you lodge the licence application. Personalised ceremonies let you choose the time, date and place and write your own vows.
2. Complete the BDM 58 form, the notice of intended marriage for couples living outside New Zealand. Sign its statutory declaration in front of an authorised person listed on the form, then send it to Births, Deaths and Marriages.
3. Time it right. The licence must be arranged at least 3 working days before the wedding and expires after 3 months.
4. Name your venue and a back-up. The ceremony can only take place at the places on your application, so for an outdoor wedding the back-up is your wet-weather plan in legal form.
5. On arrival, visit a registry office to sign a declaration before the ceremony.
6. On the day, you need 2 witnesses, and you, your celebrant and your witnesses must be physically present in the same place.
7. Afterwards, the Copy of Particulars you sign is not a marriage certificate. Order the certificate once the marriage is registered, and ask any Australian organisation receiving it whether it wants an Apostille.

Back home, you cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law.

Dreaming of alpine lakes, island vineyards or a subtropical bay? Ask your celebrant and venue who gives permission for a ceremony on a beach, in a park or on conservation land.

newsletter.subject: Get married in New Zealand: the legal steps in order
newsletter.preview: Licence, registry office visit, witnesses and your certificate: the sequence for Australian couples.
newsletter.blurb: New Zealand on your list? Our new guide sets out the legal sequence for Australian couples: the BDM 58 form signed before you leave, a licence in place at least 3 working days before the wedding, a registry office visit on arrival, your celebrant and 2 witnesses on the day, then your certificate and an Apostille if an Australian organisation asks for one. It also covers recognition in Australia, conservation land, seasons and choosing your region.
